subject: Canonical queue authorization boundary
durable_memory: Repository commits, completion narratives, evidence records, and additive queue-update files do not by themselves authorize execution. A team-owned item is executable only when present in operations/ACTIVE_QUEUE.json or another explicitly designated canonical authorization source.

observed: operations/ACTIVE_QUEUE.json contains only V-001 owned by vercel_studio.
No continuity_mining-owned item is present in the canonical queue.
CM-015 exists as an additive completed-slice queue update and states that canonical shared-state files were not overwritten.
operations/SPECIALIST_REGISTRY.json contains no registered continuity_mining specialists.
inferred: Recent continuity artifacts are committed historical evidence but are not canonical authorization for a successor run item.
Selecting a new continuity slice without a canonical item is backlog synthesis and risk containment, not execution of an authorized queue item.
proposed: Promote a successor continuity item atomically by updating the canonical queue with provenance linking the authorizing commit and predecessor evidence.
Label additive queue-update records as proposals or completion evidence until incorporated into the canonical queue.
superseded: Any interpretation that a committed operations/queue-updates record automatically modifies operations/ACTIVE_QUEUE.json.
unresolved: No atomic promotion mechanism currently binds a continuity proposal, canonical queue update, and authorizing commit in one verifiable transition.
The repository does not currently designate an alternate canonical authorization source for continuity_mining.

privacy_boundary: Repository-only operational facts; no private source material included.
